items.sentence: Bangladesh, a country in South Asia, *suffers from* terrible monsoons every year.
items.pattern: S + Appositive + Vi (Phrasal verb) + O + Adverbial phrase

items.sentence: Around one third of the country *is flooded* during the rainy season.
items.pattern: S + Passive verb phrase + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: These major floods *cause* roads to get blocked and thousands of schools to shut their doors for months at a time.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O + Infinitival phrase + and + O + Infinitival phrase

items.sentence: As a result, many children *are often denied* access to proper schooling.
items.pattern: Adverbial phrase + S + Passive verb phrase + O

items.sentence: Fortunately, an innovative architect named Mohammed Rezwan *has come up with* an appropriate and promising solution: boat schools!
items.pattern: Adverb + S + Participial phrase + Vt (Phrasal verb) + O + Appositive

items.sentence: The boat school program *was launched* in 2002 by Rezwan.
items.pattern: S + Passive verb phrase + Prepositional phrases

items.sentence: Its goal *was* to provide elementary school children in Bangladesh with education throughout the year.
items.pattern: S + Vl + Infinitival phrase (C)

items.sentence: The design of the boats *is based on* that of traditional local wooden boats called noka.
items.pattern: S + Passive phrasal verb + O + Participial phrase

items.sentence: Each boat *is* about fifteen meters long and three meters wide.
items.pattern: S + Vl + Compound C

items.sentence: On top of the boat *is* a weatherproof roof held up by arched metal beams.
items.pattern: Inverted prepositional phrase + Vi + S + Participial phrase

items.sentence: If the roof were not built with such strong materials, the boat *would be damaged* by heavy monsoon rains.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (If...) + S + Passive modal verb phrase + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: Inside, the boat school *looks* just like a regular school.
items.pattern: Adverb + S + Vl + C

items.sentence: It's *equipped with* tables, chairs, a blackboard, electronic equipment, and multimedia resources, including a computer connected to the Internet.
items.pattern: S + Passive phrasal verb + Compound O + Participial phrases

items.sentence: All the power needed on the boat *is supplied* by solar panels installed on the roof.
items.pattern: S + Participial phrase + Passive verb phrase + Prepositional phrase + Participial phrase

items.sentence: Each boat school *can accommodate* as many as thirty students and *provide* basic education up to the fourth grade.
items.pattern: S + Compound modal verb phrase + Compound O + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: Every morning, six days a week, students *wait* at the docks near their muddy villages for the boat schools to sail by and pick them up.
items.pattern: Adverbial phrases + S + Vi + Prepositional phrase + Infinitival phrase

items.sentence: Aside from traditional subjects, students also *study* environmental topics like biodiversity and water pollution.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase + S + Adverb + Vt + O

items.sentence: Each learning session *lasts* three hours.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O

items.sentence: When the session is over, each boat *takes* the students back to their village and then *sails on* to the next village to pick up another thirty students for another session.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (When...) + S + Compound verb phrase + O + Infinitival phrase

items.sentence: After school, many students *receive* low-cost solar lanterns that enable them to study at night.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase + S + Vt + O + Relative clause (that...)

items.sentence: Also, in the evenings, the boat schools *project* educational films onto large sailcloth, which allows nearby villagers to watch from the open areas outside their homes.
items.pattern: Adverbial phrases + S + Vt + O + Relative clause (which...)

items.sentence: The floating classrooms *benefit* not only children but also adults.
items.pattern: S + Vt + Correlative compound O

items.sentence: They *offer* on-board training in practical issues like nutrition, health and hygiene, and human rights.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: Boat schools also *teach* adults various farming techniques, such as growing flood-resistant crops.
items.pattern: S + Adverb + Vt + IO + DO + Exemplifying phrase

items.sentence: Such training *makes* it possible for the villagers to increase productivity so as to ensure sufficient food and year-round income.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O + C + Infinitival phrases

items.sentence: The boat schools even *offer* lessons on financial management so that people may better manage their money.
items.pattern: S + Adverb + Vt + O + Adverbial clause (so that...)

items.sentence: The boat school concept *has now been adopted* by other countries at risk of flooding, including Cambodia, Nigeria, and the Philippines.
items.pattern: S + Passive verb phrase + Prepositional phrase + Participial phrase

items.sentence: If these countries didn't have such an innovative program, they *would not be able* to rise above flood waters, overcome geographical barriers, and improve their people's lives.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (If...) + S + Modal verb phrase + Compound infinitival phrase

items.sentence: Indeed, boat classrooms *have created* opportunities for high-quality education for both children and adults.
items.pattern: Adverb + S + Vt + O + Prepositional phrases

items.sentence: By doing so, these schools *have provided* brighter futures for people living in countries that frequently suffer from severe flooding.
items.pattern: Prepositional gerund phrase + S + Vt + O + Participial phrase + Relative clause (that...)

text_genre.raw_text:
Passage Structure Analysis (Problem–Innovative Solution–Multi-Tiered Impact Pattern)
Problem & Innovative Solution (Para 1): Introduces a severe local problem (monsoon floods shutting down schools in Bangladesh) and presents the innovative solution (Mohammed Rezwan’s boat schools).
Design & Features of the Solution (Para 2): Details the physical structure, capacity, and sustainable technology (solar panels, internet-connected computers) of the boat schools.
Operation & Benefits for Primary Group (Para 3): Explains the daily schedule, curriculum (traditional + environmental topics), and evening resources (solar lanterns, film screenings) for children.
Expanded Benefits for Secondary Group (Para 4): Shows how the program also empowers adults with practical training (nutrition, flood-resistant farming, financial management).
Global Adoption & Conclusion (Para 5): Highlights the international spread of the concept and summarizes its transformative power in overcoming geographical barriers.
